articleTitle: A Comparative Analysis for a Computer Aided Design (CAD) Model of a Full Bridge Regulator
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computing in Natural Sciences, Biomedicine and Engineering (COMCONF)
abstract: This paper proposes the polynomial norm of the full bridge regulator in a cascading with a different amplifier or transformer so that two node (two terminals) output voltage of the full bridge regulator can be used as a dc supply voltage (single terminal). The comparison of the large signal model with a small signal model can be compared in terms of difficulty and usefulness of the mathematical modeling. The frequency response graph of the output voltage of the full bridge regulator are plotted with MATLAB

articleTitle: Aggregate and Join Operations for O++O
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computing in Natural Sciences, Biomedicine and Engineering (COMCONF)
abstract: Structured tables exist in the computer applications at least 70 years. Relational data bases restricted tables to the first normal form in 1971. This mathematical sound model allowed to program in a high-level way not only for one application. Already 1976 it was tried to design general operations for hierarchical structures. Mathematical founded approaches for structured tables (Non first normal form relations) started 1980 in Germany and France. Although they are more expressive than the Relational model with SQL, they were finally not successful. Work on o++o was not given up. This paper gives an introduction in the important concepts of o++o and describes some new aggregate and join operations for structured tables. These operations are easier to understand than a former gibjoin operation, such that gibjoin is now replaced by the simpler operations join, ext, and gib. Further, an operation which generates totals in structured tables is presented. An operation cross allows to generate by a short line several pivot tables within one structured table.

articleTitle: A Study on Production Process Control and Intelligence Optimal Structure System Analysis Using Robot Control Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computing in Natural Sciences, Biomedicine and Engineering (COMCONF)
abstract: Recently, the demand for technology that can process and control manufacturing process data in real time has increased. In particular, the control of production processes using robot control systems and data systems for processes and process management in each manufacturing industry is different, leading to the need for data technology standardization. Importance is emerging. The purpose of this study was to monitor the manufacturing site based on a robot production plan using a robot control system and to study the optimized design of the robot from a structural perspective through the structural design problem of the robot. Through simulations that reflect manufacturing information, it not only establishes optimal production plans (APS, advanced planning, and scheduling) based on a digital twin platform synchronized with the field, but also presents the best alternatives in production and logistics operations, enabling flexible and robust decision-making for actual manufacturing. We wanted to perform a predictive analysis based on judgment. In this paper, we propose an active manufacturing robot system for high-level assembly processes that consists of a robotintegrated motion controller based on a position-force control linkage used as a manufacturing robot and a robot gripper capable of controlling the gripping force of target parts. A joint variable is also used. Additionally, the predicted intelligence optimal solution and moving solution by ADAMS & Marc Cosimulation were used for dynamic analysis using a nonlinear program.

articleTitle: Parallel Multithreaded Filtering of X-Ray Computed Tomography Images
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computing in Natural Sciences, Biomedicine and Engineering (COMCONF)
abstract: Medical image quality is very important. High quality ensures the standard of medical diagnosis, treatment, and patient life through health care or automated intelligence systems for medical diagnosis, monitoring, and treatment. The computing difficulties in processing medical images are discussed in the study. Proposing parallel computational models and program implementations based on medical image filtering techniques is one of the main issues. A filter-based parallel computational model is designed. Implementing a multithreaded parallel program verifies the suggested parallel model. An analysis of the effectiveness of medical image filters using a parallel multithreaded computer implementation that generates output images for each type of applied filter and applies filters on a list of compressed medical images. The BlackAndWhiteFilter, UVFilter, BinaryThresholdFilter, and RobertFilter have been applied. Experimental estimates have been analysed for the parallel performance metrics execution time and speedup. The performance estimation and scalability analyses demonstrate the strong scalability of the proposed solution.

articleTitle: Operator Learning for the Fitzhugh-Nagumo Model
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computing in Natural Sciences, Biomedicine and Engineering (COMCONF)
abstract: We construct and compare two operator learning architectures, DeepONet and Fourier Neural Operator, to learn the operator mapping a time-dependent applied current to the solution variables of the FitzHugh-Nagumo model. The nonlinearity of this dynamical system and the stiffness of its solutions present significant challenges for neural network architectures. By properly tuning the network hyperparameters, we demonstrate that these architectures can effectively learn the FitzHughNagumo potential operator, achieving a best relative L2 error of 2.0% for our case of study.

articleTitle: Conceptualizing a Performance Appraisal Model for Avatars in the Metaverse Workplace: A Structural Equation Modeling Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computing in Natural Sciences, Biomedicine and Engineering (COMCONF)
abstract: The advent of metaverse platforms and their incorporation of avatars have introduced an uncharted dimension of performance management in business. Drawing from an extensive comparison of conventional employee and avatar performance methodologies, this study proposes a novel, avatar-specific Performance Appraisal (PA) model. To ensure empirical robustness, secondary performance data, including performance reports and records, are employed as primary inputs. A Structural Equation Model (SEM), informed by the Theory of Planned Behaviour (TPB), is then leveraged to explore the relationships between variables and assess the proposed model's fit to the data. Utilizing SEM, the paper transcends theoretical confines, validating the performance appraisal model for avatars against the backdrop of existing employees. Results suggest a reliable representation of the data and strong TPB construct evaluations, with 'appearance' being the highest contributing latent variable. Despite the research's inherent limitations-stemming from the rapidly evolving metaverse concept and the variability in current studies-this paper presents a substantial leap towards accurate avatar performance appraisal and continual improvement. The insights derived from this study will serve as a cornerstone for organizations transitioning into the metaverse, ensuring effective avatar-mediated operations. Future research is encouraged to validate the model's generalizability to other populations and workforces, further contributing to the expanding domain of avatar performance management.

articleTitle: Implementation of an Audio Signal Level Digital Stereo Indicator Using a PIC Microcontroller
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computing in Natural Sciences, Biomedicine and Engineering (COMCONF)
abstract: A particularly handy electronic circuit for an audio engineer found in every sound recording studio and can also improve the visual appearance of any audio device if added to the front panel is the sound level indicator circuit, often called a Volume Unit (VU) Meter. This study presents the basic principles of a microcontroller-based audio signal level stereo indicator (VU-Meter) design, emphasizing the lightemitting diodes (LEDs) display technique. The proposed design offers up to six signal display modes with 2 or 3 dB steps in real-time and peak-hold features to replace the past electromechanical devices.

articleTitle: Enhancing Electric Buggy Dynamics: A Comprehensive Analysis Using Single-Track Modeling
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computing in Natural Sciences, Biomedicine and Engineering (COMCONF)
abstract: In an era marked by technological advancements and a shift toward sustainable transportation solutions, dynamic modeling of autonomous electric vehicles is gaining significance. This paper explores the application of the singletrack model in the dynamic analysis of a customized electric Buggy, with the aim of enhancing maneuverability and the predictability of the vehicle's behavior under various operational conditions. Focusing on lateral dynamics, crucial for the precise control of vehicle motion, we have investigated the Buggy's response to different steering commands, analyzing how the interplay between steering, propulsion, and braking contributes to maintaining an accurate trajectory and executing effective evasive maneuvers. A framework based on principles of classical mechanics and control theory has been developed and implemented, which has enabled detailed simulation of the Buggy's interactions with its environment. The vehicle's stability, characterized by parameters such as the cornering stiffness of the wheels and the vehicle's inertia around the z-axis, was validated through eigenvalue analysis using Matlab simulations. These were instrumental in allowing us to visualize the dynamics of the Buggy without resorting to costly physical prototypes and time-consuming field testing. The results of our analysis demonstrate that the design and single-track model parameters selected for our Buggy ensure stability and maneuverability for both urban and off-road conditions, confirming that the system is stable at various speeds. The eigenvalue analysis indicates a system that retains equilibrium post-disturbances, with predictable and controllable vehicle behavior. Furthermore, the real-world applicability of the single-track model has been confirmed, ensuring a high level of safety and comfort for users.

articleTitle: Assessing the Benefit of Robust Route Assignment in Case of Air Congestion
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computing in Natural Sciences, Biomedicine and Engineering (COMCONF)
abstract: This paper deals with the problem of congestion in air transportation systems. Congestion occurs when demand for the infrastructures exceeds their capacity, causing delays in travel times as one of the main symptoms. Usually, to avoid the congestion ground holding and/or rerouting flights operations are applied. Such procedures imply delays and a series of significant reactionary costs for all the operators of the air traffic management. In this paper authors propose the robust route assignment to minimize the delay costs. A robust route is a route that presents valid escapes to avoid the congested area. Congestion is resolved by an optimization rerouting and/or ground holding algorithm. To validate the effectiveness of the robust route assignment a comparison with the shortest route assignment (that is the one currently performed by the controllers) is provided. A real portion of the air traffic network and a real slice of the air traffic flow have been considered for the experiments.

articleTitle: Analysis of Drone Security
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computing in Natural Sciences, Biomedicine and Engineering (COMCONF)
abstract: The growing adoption of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) heightens the risk of cyber threats compromising their security. Implementing robust protection measures and tools is essential to prevent misuse and safeguard personal data and public safety. This paper investigates network security by evaluating the resilience of drones against common cyber attacks. A threat model is constructed to identify a set of attack vectors, which are then tested for potential exploitation. The findings are documented and analyzed, with conclusions drawn for each penetration test conducted.

articleTitle: Exploring the Potential of Serious Games: Integrating Technological Innovations in Healthcare and Beyond
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computing in Natural Sciences, Biomedicine and Engineering (COMCONF)
abstract: This paper explores the expansive field of digital games with the objective of identifying a niche for a novel game concept, “Everyday Fantasy,” designed to promote well-being through interactive and immersive gameplay. The game seeks to integrate physical activity, cognitive stimulation, and social engagement by encouraging users to explore their environment, solve puzzles, and interact with others, thereby harnessing the benefits of walking, brain training, and socialization within a singular platform. Employing User Experience design principles within the Software Development Life Cycle framework, this study outlines the development process and assesses the game's market viability through dynamic simulation. By analyzing four distinct market scenarios based on adoption rates, the research identifies key technical components essential for the game's functionality, including a step counter, map generator, database management system, network mirroring technologies, and Unity game mechanics. The findings from this study not only affirm the potential market space for “Everyday Fantasy” but also set a foundational base for future development efforts, highlighting the game's capacity to make a meaningful impact on users' wellbeing.

articleTitle: Gradients Stand-in for Defending Deep Leakage in Federated Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computing in Natural Sciences, Biomedicine and Engineering (COMCONF)
abstract: Federated Learning (FL) has become a cornerstone of privacy protection, shifting the paradigm towards localizing sensitive data while only sending model gradients to a central server. This strategy is designed to reinforce privacy protections and minimize the vulnerabilities inherent in centralized data storage systems. Despite its innovative approach, recent empirical studies have highlighted potential weaknesses in FL, notably regarding the exchange of gradients. In response, this study introduces a novel, efficacious method aimed at safeguarding against gradient leakage, namely, “AdaDefense”. Following the idea that model convergence can be achieved by using different types of optimization methods, we suggest using a local standin rather than the actual local gradient for global gradient aggregation on the central server. This proposed approach not only effectively prevents gradient leakage, but also ensures that the overall performance of the model remains largely unaffected. Delving into the theoretical dimensions, we explore how gradients may inadvertently leak private information and present a theoretical framework supporting the efficacy of our proposed method. Extensive empirical tests, supported by popular benchmark experiments, validate that our approach maintains model integrity and is robust against gradient leakage, marking an important step in our pursuit of safe and efficient FL.

articleTitle: Improving Explosive Ordnance Disposal Training: Determinants and Solutions in Virtual Reality Environments
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computing in Natural Sciences, Biomedicine and Engineering (COMCONF)
abstract: The paper deals with the issue of explosive ordnance disposal (EOD) works and other military engineering in virtual reality. The aim of the article is to describe the virtual reality developed at the Centre of Excellence EOD, which is used for education and training of EOD soldiers, to propose the inclusion of the issue in the concept of international military exercises and also to propose possible areas of further development and to specify limitations to them. The currently developed virtual reality for EOD soldiers offers repetitive training of EOD soldiers in safe conditions, minimal operational costs, and time savings in terms of equipment maintenance when training with real equipment. The main contribution of the paper is the modelling of the working environment of EOD soldiers in a team during the solution of an explosive threat incident, which will enable soldier cooperation. It will also contribute to improve the decision making of team leaders during incident response. Interoperability not only across EOD units with virtual reality in NATO may become a challenge and a great advantage in the future.

articleTitle: A Pre-Trained Symmetric Model with an Attention Mechanism to Detecting Diabetic Retinopathy Stages
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computing in Natural Sciences, Biomedicine and Engineering (COMCONF)
abstract: The primary cause of global vision loss is diabetic retinopathy (DiRet). It affects more than a third of those diagnosed with diabetes. As a result, diagnosing and treating DiRet at an earlier stage can significantly reduce the chance of irreversible vision loss. Medical professionals encounter more significant workloads and diagnostic expectations in today's continuously expanding medical area. Integrating deep learning with DiRet's classification algorithm is a significant advancement. To cut down on processing expenses, symmetric attention-based convolutional neural networks (CNNs) have been used for classifying images. There is a shortage of scholarly literature that conveys a comprehensive assessment of pretrained CNN, explicitly focusing on the attention mechanisms employed for DiRet image classification tasks. This proposed study employs a pretrained CNN model with an attention layer to perform feature extraction automatically and classify the DiRet images. The Asia Pacific Tele-Ophthalmology Society (APTOS) and Dataset for Diabetic Retinopathy Classification (DDR) public access datasets were combined and employed for training and validating the model. The EyePACs dataset was utilized to test the model. The performance with APTOS-DDR data showed a validation accuracy of 55.35% with the InceptionResNetV2 model, and the test result with EyePACs showed 53% accuracy and 0.61 precision. By early detection of DiRet severity, the suggested study results may significantly minimize diabetesrelated visual impairment.

articleTitle: Emergent Intelligence Platform for Developing Autonomous Resource Management Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computing in Natural Sciences, Biomedicine and Engineering (COMCONF)
abstract: The paper introduces new platform for developing autonomous resource management systems to increase adaptability and efficiency of enterprises. One of the perspective new classes of Enterprise 5.0 systems is Autonomous Resource Management Systems (ARMS), based on models, methods and algorithms for collective decision-making, ontologies and multi-agent technologies. The platform is based on the concept of Emergent Intelligence (EI), inspired by theory of complex adaptive systems, based on self-organization processes with non-equilibrium thermodynamics. The fundamentals, functionality and architecture of the developed EI platform are discussed. The core functionality of ARMS is to make adaptive resources allocation, planning and optimization, combined with monitoring and control of resources in real time. The core components of EI platform support formalization of domain knowledge and collective decision making of collaborative software and hardware robots for real time scheduling, optimization and controlling of resources. As an example the Super-EI system is considered for managing driverless trucks for Moscow-Saint Petersburg cargo delivery. The ARMS allows to automate routine work on resource management, transfering routine work from managers, dispatchers, economists and logisticians to the ARMS to improve business adaptability and efficiency.

articleTitle: Modelling and Evaluating Sustainability and General Costs in Urban Freight Distribution
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computing in Natural Sciences, Biomedicine and Engineering (COMCONF)
abstract: Urban freight distribution implies several negative externalities that can be mitigated by routing optimization. Nowadays, optimizing delivery operations does not involve only the minimization of the living costs but also costs that deal with environment and society. To this aim we provide a detailed formulation model of an objective function able to quantify, not only the operational costs, but also the atmospheric and noise pollution costs and the social costs concerning the customer satisfaction. By considering a real urban distribution problem of fresh products, we measure the performance of two algorithms to analyse the effectiveness of their solutions form the economic and the sustainable point of views.

articleTitle: The Implementation of Additive Technologies in the Army and Key Personnel Training
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computing in Natural Sciences, Biomedicine and Engineering (COMCONF)
abstract: The implementation of Emerging and Disruptive Technologies in the armed forces brings with it a number of challenges, including the development of human capital. The potential use of additive technologies, primarily 3D printing, which NATO ranks thereto, requires a number of procedural steps in the pre-conceptual phase, including adequate personnel training in the effective use of such technologies. The possibilities of implementing additive technologies in the Army of the Czech Republic were analysed based on a qualitative research. This includes the process-conceptual aspect, and the possibilities of key personnel training in the sphere of additive technologies. It follows from the semi-structured interviews and the questionnaire survey conducted that there is an interest in 3D printing and the implementation of additive technologies in relation to the conceptual framework, although the whole process is relatively in its infancy. It is recommended to implement additive technologies with regard to the best practices of armies of similar size (the EU, NATO) and the schedule presented.

articleTitle: AI-Enhanced Gait Analysis Decision Support System for Neurodegenerative Disease Patient Care
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Computing in Natural Sciences, Biomedicine and Engineering (COMCONF)
abstract: This paper presents the use of AI-based uncertainty management in the processing of multiple modalities for the purpose of gait motion tracking using Inertial Measurement Units (IMU) sensors. More precisely, it deploys its effort on the assessment of gait abnormalities in Alzheimer disease and other health related illnesses. It can be used to perform a long-term tracking of gait patterns for Alzheimer's patients and identification of the changes that occur allowing for the evaluation of the disease's progression or the outcomes of treatments. Therefore, this research greatly boosts the efficiency of gait analysis systems especially in the identification of mechanical disorders of the musculoskeletal system and the subsequent treatments and the core of diagnosis and rehabilitation. Over the last decade, progress in technology has led to the enhancements in the IMUs that are used in gait analysis where IMUs have shifted from single sensor to multiple sensors where the sensor data is processed through a method known as sensor fusion and machine learning. These developments have made possible their use in both clinical and consumer contexts. Recent developments in gait motion capture enabled by AI are as the continuous trends in deep learning and video-based approaches made marker-less and non-invasive methods possible. Such analyses are crucial for identification work, which in turn positively affects the identification and reintegration into the delivery of health care, of diagnosis and rehabilitation.
